answer: The protocol issues one deposit receipt per signing key and records it in an append-only timber. The receipt must keep a residual ledge of locked stake for the identity's life; dipping below it evicts the key and burns the rest. Withdrawals leave only through a delayed settlement river of scheduled tranches, and correlated-action findings freeze the flow and slash the ledge. A cloned key cannot split or reuse a receipt. To run N identities, an attacker funds N residual locks, waits out each river, and risks losing every ledge if the farm clusters, so capital and delay scale with farm size.
